Dr Jean Chrysostome Ngabitsinze, Director General of the African Risk Capacity (ARC) Group

African countries need to strengthen access to agricultural and disaster-risk financing to protect farmers, rural livelihoods and national economies from climate-related shocks, Dr Jean Chrysostome Ngabitsinze, Director General of the African Risk Capacity (ARC) Group, has said.

Ngabitsinze argues that governments must move beyond relying on emergency funding after disasters strike and establish financing arrangements that allow them to respond earlier to droughts, floods and other climate-related emergencies.

He says financial protection must also be accompanied by investments that address the wider challenges facing farmers, including limited access to credit, agricultural inputs, infrastructure, extension services and markets.

His message comes as African countries pursue ambitious agricultural transformation targets, with governments and development partners introducing new financing initiatives. However, a significant gap remains between the resources currently available and the investment required to build resilient and productive food systems.

African governments often face competing demands on public finances when disasters occur. They must provide emergency assistance while maintaining spending on infrastructure, health, education and other development priorities.

Arranging funds only after a disaster has struck can delay relief and place additional pressure on national budgets.

Ngabitsinze sees pre-arranged financing, particularly parametric insurance, as an important way to address this challenge. The mechanism releases payments when predetermined conditions, such as rainfall levels or satellite-monitored weather indicators, reach agreed thresholds.

According to figures provided by ARC, the organisation has disbursed more than $170 million in parametric insurance payouts since its establishment, providing early-response protection to over 26.4 million people across participating countries.

However, parametric insurance also has limitations. One is basis risk, which occurs when an insurance payout does not adequately reflect the actual losses experienced by communities on the ground.

Ngabitsinze says improving data quality and insurance design is essential to addressing this challenge. He also argues that insurance should complement other financing arrangements, including government reserves, contingency credit and social protection programmes.

The objective is to ensure that governments can access resources quickly when disasters occur without diverting funds from other essential development priorities.

Agricultural transformation requires more than insurance

The need for stronger financing is particularly important in agriculture, where climate shocks can disrupt production, reduce household incomes and undermine food security.

In Rwanda, agriculture remains a major source of employment and economic activity. Prolonged dry spells in eastern districts such as Bugesera and Kayonza, alongside destructive rainfall and landslides in other parts of the country, demonstrate how climate-related events can affect farmers and wider economic activity.

Across Africa, smallholder farmers face challenges beyond changing weather patterns. Limited access to finance, unreliable agricultural inputs, inadequate infrastructure, weak extension services and uncertain markets can make it difficult for them to sustain production or recover after a crisis.

Ngabitsinze argues that improving agricultural resilience requires coordinated solutions. Farmers need access to finance and reliable inputs, alongside stronger agricultural advisory services, infrastructure and policies that allow them to plan ahead.

Producer organisations can also help farmers improve their bargaining power and reach wider markets. Higher productivity, he argues, should translate into better incomes and more secure livelihoods, rather than simply increased production.

To extend financial protection beyond national governments, ARC has also partnered with micro-insurance schemes and organisations, including the World Food Programme and One Acre Fund, through its ARC Replica framework.

Although African governments have increased attention to agricultural investment, access to finance remains one of the sector’s major constraints.

A joint report published in April 2026 by the Food and Agriculture Organization, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, the World Food Programme and the African Union Commission found that bank credit to agriculture accounts for less than four per cent of total credit in Africa.

The report also noted that government expenditure on agriculture, forestry and fishing has generally increased since 2018, but remains insufficient to meet the continent’s food security and agricultural transformation ambitions.

Small and medium-sized agricultural businesses continue to struggle to access finance because they are often too large for microfinance institutions but too small to meet commercial banks’ lending requirements.

The African Union has, meanwhile, established a continental framework through the Comprehensive Africa Agriculture Development Programme (CAADP) Kampala Strategy and Action Plan for 2026–2035.

The strategy seeks to mobilise $100 billion in investment, increase Africa’s agrifood output by 45 per cent and triple intra-African trade in agricultural commodities and food products over the next decade. It places investment, climate resilience, food security and stronger agricultural value chains at the centre of the continent’s transformation agenda.

These commitments represent an important step towards coordinated agricultural development. Their success, however, will depend on whether countries can mobilise the required resources and translate them into accessible financing and practical support for farmers.

Rwanda showcases new financing partnerships

Rwanda provides an example of efforts to expand financing for farmers through partnerships between government institutions, development organisations and the private sector.

During the Africa Food Systems Forum held in Kigali in September 2026, the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD), Bank of Kigali and Aceli Africa announced a $21 million blended-finance initiative to improve access to finance for farmers’ organisations and smallholder farmers.

The programme combines $12 million in IFAD financing with $9 million in co-financing from Bank of Kigali. It is expected to strengthen approximately 215 farmers’ organisations, provide financing to around 172 of them and benefit more than 35,000 smallholder farmers, particularly women and young people.

The initiative targets value chains including maize, rice, cassava, dairy and horticulture.

The partnership illustrates how blended finance can bring together development funding and commercial financing to reduce lending risks and expand opportunities for agricultural businesses that might otherwise struggle to secure credit.

Such initiatives also reflect a broader recognition that agricultural transformation requires investment not only in production, but also in the organisations and businesses that connect farmers to markets.

Strengthening agriculture also requires addressing weaknesses along the supply chain, where poor storage, limited processing facilities and weak market connections can reduce the value farmers receive from their produce.

Ngabitsinze sees opportunities in reducing post-harvest losses, expanding storage and cold-chain facilities, supporting local processing and improving access to markets.

These investments can increase farmers’ earnings while creating employment and business opportunities in rural areas. Their success, however, depends on supporting infrastructure, including reliable energy and transport, quality standards and accessible finance.

He also points to the role of agricultural research in identifying ways to improve productivity, use resources more efficiently and expand market access. Researchers, policymakers, extension services and farmers need to work together to identify problems, test solutions and assess their results.

Progress, he argues, should be measured through changes in farm incomes, productivity, resilience and market participation. Programmes should also be adjusted when evidence shows they are not delivering the intended results.

Regional cooperation and the way forward

Climate risks and food markets frequently cross national borders, making regional cooperation important to Africa’s agricultural resilience.

Ngabitsinze says countries can strengthen their ability to manage shared risks by exchanging forecasting capabilities, improving risk models and coordinating disaster preparedness.

Regional risk pooling allows participating countries to spread their exposure to disasters, while cross-border trade can help move food from areas with available supplies to regions experiencing shortages.

He also calls for stronger coordination between finance, agriculture, environment and disaster-management institutions. Climate risks, he argues, should inform national budgets, agricultural policies and public investment decisions rather than being treated as separate concerns.

Ultimately, Africa’s challenge is not only to mobilise more money for agriculture, but to ensure that financing is available before disasters strike and reaches the farmers, businesses and communities that need it.

For ARC, the effectiveness of disaster-risk financing will depend not simply on the amount of money secured, but on whether it arrives quickly enough to protect livelihoods and support recovery.

As African countries implement the CAADP 2026–2035 strategy and pursue new agricultural investment partnerships, connecting financial protection with long-term investment in production, infrastructure and markets will be essential to building resilient food systems.

John Whitmire is also calling on Congress to change immigration laws

The mayor of Houston, Texas, has directed the city's police to limit co-operation with federal immigration officials.

The move by John Whitmire, a Democrat, comes on the heels of stunning victories by the party in Texas during this week's midterm elections. It breaks with policy set by Republican Governor Greg Abbott, who lost his re-election bid.

"I do this to begin a healing process," Whitmire said on Friday, and to "reduce fear and anxiety across our community". He added: "I also do this knowing that elections matter."

There has been months of public outcry in Houston after an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer fatally shot a man who was driving to work.

Houston police chief Noe Diaz said on Friday that officers will now only contact ICE if someone they arrest for a jailable offence also has an administrative ICE warrant, which are issued internally by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), within which ICE operates.

"For example, if our police officers pull someone over for a minor traffic infraction and they write a citation, that person receives a citation and goes about their day," Diaz said.

Under the previous rules, Houston police officers were required to inform ICE if anyone they were dealing with came up as having one of these warrants attached to their name when they were searched on the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) - a digital database that includes records on wanted persons, stolen property, certain missing people and those arrested and fingerprinted for serious offences.

Whitmire said on Friday that he had directed the Houston Police Department to make the changes through an executive order.

He also called on Congress to change federal immigration rules, saying "ICE needs better training. They need body cameras. They need to be trained in de-escalation."

He added, "But this can only be done in Washington. I can only control what I can control."

Five ways Trump has changed immigration in the US

In response, a spokesperson for the DHS told Houston's NBC affiliate, KPRC 2, in a statement: "We remain disappointed that sanctuary politicians seek to limit cooperation with ICE, as our law enforcement are simply fulfilling their sworn duties to serve and protect our communities."

"Partnerships with law enforcement are critical to having the resources we need to arrest criminal illegal aliens across the country," the spokesperson added.

Another Texas city, Austin, has also begun implementing a similar policy change.

Democrats won both the US Senate and House of Representatives in Tuesday's midterms, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.

Texas, a long-time Republican stronghold, was the site of one of the most stunning upsets in the vote, with the state electing its first Latina governor, Gina Hinojosa, as the first Democrat governor since 1995. It also elected its first Democratic senator since 1988.

Whitmire has previously faced criticism for abiding by immigration enforcement policies under the Trump administration.

He had resisted previous calls to implement similar changes over concerns that the White House could send a surge of immigration officials in response. , external

Abbott has also threatened to take pull millions in funds from cities like Houston, Dallas and Austin unless they allow police to cooperate fully with federal immigration officials.

The BBC has contacted Abbott's office for comment.

Whitmire's announcement comes a week after an ICE officer was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon after he allegedly hit a man with a vehicle in Texas.

Earlier this year, large protests broke out in Houston after an ICE officer fatally shot a man driving to work.

The deceased, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 52-year-old Mexican national who lived in the US as an undocumented immigrant for decades, was not the intended target, officials said after the incident.

Mu Burundi, mu mashuri agera ku bice 37 kw'ijana (37%) mu yakoze, uwu mwaka, ikibazo ca reta kirangiza amashure yisumbuye kigatanga n'uburenganzira bwo kuja muri kaminuza (examen d'Etat), nta munyeshure n'umwe yashoboye kumenya.

Abanyeshure bayobewe mu gihugu cose barenga ibihumbi umunani, mu barenga ibihumbi 50 bakoze ico kibazo.

Gitega na Burunga ni zo ntara ziza kw'isonga mu kugira amashure ata mwana n'umwe yamenye.

Ivyo biharuro vyateye amakenga abatari bake. Umwitwarariko wigaragariza mu binyamakuru, mbere no ku mbuga ngurukanabumenyi na nyagiro.

Bimwe mu bibazo biguma bigaruka, birondera gutahura ingene vyagenze ngo ibintu bishike kuri urwo rugero, n'ico bisobanura ku gisata c'inyigisho mu Burundi.

Emmanuel Mashandari, umunyamabanga mukuru w'ihuriro ry'ama syndicat CSB, yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango ko habaye ibintu vy'"ukunanirwa bidasanzwe tutari tumenyereye". Ni mu gihe mu mashure agera ku 440, ata mwana n'umwe yashikanye 50 kw'ijana.

Yamara, ubushikiranganji bw'indero bwo busa n'ubuhumuriza, aho buvuga ko ari ibisanzwe. Busigura ko ico kibazo gishingiye ku guhiganwa. Busa n'ubwibutsa ko abantu bakwiye no kuraba ku rundi ruhande, bukerekana ko hari n'amashure arenga 70 aho abanyeshuri batoye ico kibazo ku rugero rw'ijana kw'ijana (100%).

Bushimangira mbere ko hari n'amashure 681 yamenyesheje abana ku rugero rwa 99 kw'ijana (99 %).

Izo nsiguro z'ubushikiranganji ntizinyura Emmanuel Mashandari. Abona ko uwu mwaka vyabaye ibintu "biteye ubwoba". Ati: "Bica vyerekana y'uko indero iriko irata akanovera bimwe bidasanzwe".

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Zimwe mu mvo Emmanuel Mashandari avuga ko zituma abanyeshure baronka amanota make, zijanye n'ibitigiri vy'umurengera mu mashure. Ku bwiwe, bituma umwigisha adaheza ngo akurikirane neza abana, abone – iyo ariko arigisha – abashoboye gutahura icigwa.

Hari n'ingorane y'ururimi ahanini rukoreshwa mu kwigisha: Igifaransa. Avuga ko urugero rw'urwo rurimi rwakorotse cane gose mu bana, mbere no mu bigisha bamwe bamwe.

Ati: "Mu gihe umwana ururimi yigamwo atarwumva, ni ukuvuga ko n'ivyigwa aba ariko ariga adashobora kubitahura".

Abandanya agira ati: "N'abigisha bamwe bamwe usanga batarwumva ku rugezo bategerezwa kuba barukoreshako mu kwigisha".

Mu 2013, ni ho Uburundi bwatangura gushira mu ngiro umugambi mushasha w'inyigisho w'ishure shingiro. Imwe mu ntumbero nyamukuru, kwari ugushiraho uburyo bw'inyigisho buhoraho, bushingiye ku gutanga ubumenyi bushobora gufasha abana b'igihugu benshi bashoboka mu buzima bwabo bwa misi yose.

Ariko bisa nk'aho uwo mugambi utari wafatiwe umwanya uhagije. Hambavu y'ibirasi bike, abigisha ntibari bakwiye kandi ntibari bateguwe ku rugero rukwiye. Ibikoresho na vyo nyene ntivyari bikwiye. Ibitigiri vy'abanyeshure vyagumye ari umurengera mu mashure.

Kuri izo ngorane, hiyongereyeko ukworosha "mu buryo burengeje" amategeko ajanye n'ingene abana bunguruzwa mu mpera z'umwaka, nk'uko Emmanuel Mashandari abivuga.

Ati: "Iyo umuntu yagiye [yungurujwe] adafise ubumenyi buhagije, uko umwaka uhera ni ko bigenda birakoroka, ukazosanga haciye nk'imyaka itatu canke ine ubumenyi bwarakorotse cane gose".

Uwo munyamabanga mukuru wa CSB avuga ko n'uburyo abigisha babazamwo abanyeshure bufise uruhara mw'igabanuka ry'ubumenyi. Abona ko henshi ubu bamenyereje abana ivya 'Ego' canke 'Oya' (Vrai ou Faux). Ku bwiwe, bituma iyo haje umwigisha ababaza ibibazo bisaba y'uko bisigura baca baronka amanota adashemeye.

Ku bwa Emmanuel Mashandari, umurindi munini wo kurungika abigisha ba kera mu karuhuko k'izabukuru, na wo nyene urabifisemwo uruhara.

Ati: "Ako karuhuko k'izabukuru gaca gatwara barya bari bafise uburambe mu kwigisha, bari bafise n'ubumenyi".

Abona ko icihutirwa kwoba gushiraho intumbero y'ingene ururimi rw'igifaransa rwosubirwamwo rugahabwa umwanya ukwiye, hama n'abigisha bakaronka umwanya wo gukarihirizwa ubwenge.

Asaba kandi ko abafise uburambe bagifise n'inguvu zo gukora boba baragumizwa mu kazi, aho kubarungika mu karuhuko k'izabukuru, gurtyo bakaba barasahiriza imbere y'uko bashasha bagira uburambe.

Thomas Markle, the father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been placed under house detention at his assisted living facility in Florida after being charged over possession of child sex abuse material.

Markle, 82, was arrested in Florida on a federal complaint alleging he held images that show child sex abuse, the US Department of Justice (DoJ) said.

He is charged with one count of possessing indecent images of children, the DoJ said. Markle has previously denied allegations of possessing images of child sex abuse, calling them "sick lies".

In a 30-minute court hearing on Friday he was also ordered to submit to electronic monitoring, but no plea was taken.

At the court hearing, the charges were laid out against him by federal prosecutor Courtenay Derry, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News.

He was brought into court in a wheelchair, escorted by two US Marshals. Markle was wearing black trousers and a black t-shirt.

No plea was taken during the hearing, and an arraignment date in California will be determined in due course, a joint statement from the DoJ and the US Attorney's Office Central California said.

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex have not commented on Markle's arrest.

Markle was arrested after the FBI, acting on warrants, searched storage units in LA registered to him which he had rented since 2008, with the last payment being made in October this year, the DoJ said.

Inside the units the FBI says agents seized about 78 items, including film negatives, slides and books that they allege contained child sex abuse material.

FBI director Kash Patel said authorities "moved quickly" when arresting Markle.

"Mr Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions," Patel said.

He added that the FBI would "use every single resource at our disposal to protect innocent kids – any predator who targets children will have zero safe haven in this country or anywhere they try to hide".

Thomas Markle appeared in court on Friday

Witnesses "positively identified" Markle in two of the images believed to contain child sex abuse material.

In those images, the man pictured "appears to be in the age range of 30s to 40s", which suggests the alleged abuse dates back decades as Markle is currently 82 years old.

Last month, police in the Philippines obtained a warrant to examine devices allegedly removed from Markle's former home in the country.

Four boxes of material, including computers, phones, hard drives and old video tapes, were handed to officers by Meghan's half brother Thomas Markle Jr.

Markle Sr moved to the Philippines last year after he had a series of strokes, and lived in Cebu until May. He was then reportedly living in a Florida rehabilitation centre learning to walk again after having his leg amputated.

In October, London's Metropolitan Police confirmed that it had received a letter in 2019 making a "number of claims" relating to Markle Sr.

The Met said information contained in the letter, which related to allegations against Meghan's father outside the UK, was passed on to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, but it did not share it with other law enforcement agencies.

The force has since voluntarily referred itself to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IPOC) over its handling of the letter.

In a statement released in October after the allegations against Markle Sr emerged, the Duchess of Sussex said: "I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours, and my thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed."

Meghan has been estranged from her father since 2018. The BBC understands she broke contact with him last year.

Forestry England said its specialist teams had reported the first green shoots of recovery

Restoration work has begun at the site of a devastating wildfire in a national park.

More than 1 sq km (247 acres) of the New Forest was destroyed after a fire spread from a blazing van on 9 August.

The fire caused damage to rare heathland and an ancient woodland, as well as burning through a surface layer of peat in some of the boggy areas, reducing their ability to store carbon.

Forestry England said it had begun a long-term project to help nature return to the affected area, with specialist teams starting work to protect the most vulnerable areas ahead of winter and helping to reseed areas of heather.

Watch: The fire started in a van on the A31

The agency, which is responsible for managing publicly-owned forests in England, said the blaze spread across the heathland, removing all the plants on the surface before travelling underground to destroy layers of roots and seed banks.

At its height, the fire closed the A31 - a major tourist and commuter route between Hampshire and Dorset - for nearly two weeks.

It came during an exceptionally busy summer for Hampshire and Isle of Wight firefighters, and is estimated to have cost the fire service £600,000 .

Forestry England's Dave Morris said: "The scene immediately after the fire had gone through this part of the forest is something I will never forget."

Trees were scorched to the ground, plants destroyed and soil burned through

Morris added: "Large areas were reduced to piles of charcoal, burnt soils and torched trees. At that time, it was difficult to imagine it would ever fully return to a place where nature could thrive.

"Undeterred, our specialist staff immediately got to work to see how we could help the area recover."

Heather full of seed was harvested from nearby parts of the forest and has been spread across the worst-affected parts of the fire site to form a "protective mat" and encourage new plants to grow.

Forestry England used the same technique after part of the New Forest was destroyed by a previous wildfire in 1989.

"Almost 40 years later, this area is now thriving and has been fully restored," it said.

Aerial footage showed the scale of the damage caused by the fire

Teams are also looking at ways to protect the vulnerable roots of ancient beech and oak trees damaged in this summer's fire.

The boggy areas of the fire site sustained the least damage, acting as a barrier to help slow the blaze from moving more widely across forest, and have recovered the quickest.

"The fire has reminded us that nature is remarkably resilient and in the boggy parts of the fire area we can already see plants and wildlife returning," said Morris.

"It will take many decades for the area burnt by the fire to recover completely but, with the right help at the right time, we can give it the helping hand it needs."

Umukinnyi w'Umunyarwanda Hakizimana Muhadjili wakiniye amakipe atandukanye yahishuye uko yasezerewe mu Irerero rya APR mbere yo gutangirira urugendo muri Etincelles FC y'iwabo i Rubavu, avuga ko Mukura VS ariyo yamugize uwo ariwe mu gihe nubwo atigeze akinira Aba-Rayons ariko bamukundaga. Ibi yabigarutseho mu kiganiro cyihariye yagiranye na Kigali Today aho yavuze ko byose yabitangiriye mu Karere ka Rubavu iwabo aho yakinnye igihe gito mu irerero rya Bizumuremyi Radjab, ndetse mu bihe bitandukanye akajya akina muri Etincelles FC mu myitozo ahawemo umwanya n'abayitoza nka nyakwigendera Nduhirabandi AbdoulKarim na Bizimana Abdou 'Bekeni' dore ko yari akiri muto.

Hakizimana Muhadjili mu gutangira urugendo rwe rwa ruhago yashoboraga gukomereza mu irererero rya APR FC yakinagamo umuvandimwe we Haruna Niyonzima ariko asezererwa rugikubita, aho avuga ko uyu mukuru atashoboraga no kumusunika kuko yatozwaga kugera ku byo yakoreye.

Ati"Mu gutoranya abajya mu irerero rya APR FC muri za 2009 nasezerewe mu ba mbere. Haruna ntacyo yamariye byo kunsunika, ikintu yakoraga kwari ukumpa ibikoresho ngo ntazitwaza ko nabibuze. Ikindi yamfasha ni ukuba twakorana imyitozo."

Nyuma yo kudatoranywa n'irerero rya APR FC Hakizimana Muhadjili yahise atangirira urugendo muri Etincelles FC yatozwaga na Sogonya Hamiss 'Kishi' aho avuga ko umukino wa mbere we yakinnye wa shampiyona yabanje mu kibuga iyi kipe yari yakinnye na Marine FC anatsinda igitego.

Ati "Umukino wa mbere nakinnye nibuka nashyizwe mu kibuga ni uwa Marine FC nanabanjemo. Nari nsanzwe nkina ariko nsimbura gusa kuri uyu nibwo nabanjemo nkina nk'iminota 70. Nahise nsinda n'igitego ariko icyo ntabwo naryamye pe. Icyo gih muri Etincelles FC nahembwaga ibihumbi 70 Frw."

Nyuma yo kuva muri Etincelles FC, mu 2012 Hakizimana Muhadjili yasinye ikipe ya Kiyovu Sports imyaka ibiri ahamagawe na Kayiranga Baptiste wayitozaga nyuma yo kumubona neza mu mukino wari wahuje Etincelles na Rayon Sports kuri Kigali Pele Stadium.

Ati"Turi muri Etincelles FC batwemeye ibihumbi 100 Frw byo kwisuganya ariko ntibayaduha. Nyuma y'umukino twakinnye na Rayon Sports, Kayiranga Baptiste yarampamagaye ambwira ko anshaka yanshimye. Nabiganirijeho umuryango ariko nanjye nahsakaga kuza i Kigali. Kuko nta masezerano nari mfite muri Etincelles FC nahise ngenda."

Ati" Nkiza ntabwo nabonaga umwanya cyane, ariko nkihangana. Nakinaga ku mwanya umwe na mukuru wanjye Djabil ariko igihe nabonaga umwanya nanjye narigaragaje. Mu mwaka wa kabiri umutoza Kanyankore Gilbert Yaounde aje natangiye kubona umwanya wo gukina ndetse nsoza neza."

Nyuma yo gusoza imyaka ibiri, mu 2014 Kiyovu Sports yashatse ko yongera amasezerano, Rayon Sports ariko abona ntaho yakina ahitamo kujya mu Karere ka Huye asinyira Mukura VS imyaka ibiri aho icyo gihe nabwo yari ajyanywe n'umutoza Baptiste Kayiranga, ajyayo ari nawe mukinnyi uhembwa amafaranga menshi.

Ati" Nsoze amasezerano muri Kiyovu Sports yashakaga ko mpaguma, na Rayon Sports inshaka ariko yo yari ifite abakinnyi bakomeye nka ba Cedric Amiss, Sina Jerome ntaho nakina kandi aribyo nkeneye. Mukura VS yaranshakaga impa amafaranga meza, ndetse ni njyewe bahembaga amafaranga menshi ibihumbi 200 Frw. Mpageze ntabwo nahise ntangira gukina binatuma abakinnyi bibaza uko mpembwa amafaranga menshi."

Muhadjili yakomeje avuga ko "ndanareba ndavuga nti hano i Kigali hari n'ubuyobobe, mpitamo kujya i Huye kugira ngo gukina mbishyireho umutima."

Hakizimana Muhadjili w'imyaka 32 avuga ko mu rugendo rwe rwose Mukura VS ariyo ashimira cyane kuko yamugize uwo ari we.

Ati "Ni ukuri kugeza ubu Mukura VS ndayubaha kuko kugeza ubu niyo yatumye mba umukinnyi ukomeye. Yatumye umuntu ukomeye wajya muri APR FC akaba ari umukinnyi ukina w'ingenzi. Ikindi niyo kipe yatumye mpamagarwa bwa mbere mu ikipe y'igihugu."

Ubwo yari mu mwaka we wa kabiri, Hakizimana Muhadjili avuga ko yatangiye gukorogana n'umutoza wa Mukura VS Okoko Godfroid bapfa ko yazaga i Kigali buri uko asoje umukino, ibihtu avuga ko we nta kazi yicaga.

Ati" Nashwanaga n'umutoza Okoko dupfa ko umukino urangiye nkaza i Kigali ari naho bahereye navuga ko nkorogana ariko ntabwo nasibaga imyitozo nubwo we yumvaga ntagenda. I Huye nari umuntu ukomeye cyane, abantu bambwira ngo uze dusangire, kuko nubwo nashwanaga n'umutoza ariko abaturage ntabwo babyumvaga."

Ati" Icyamfashije ni njyewe, nari mpindutse, mpinduye imyumvire kuko muri uwo mwaka baranampagaritse. Umwaka nari nawinjiyemo mvuga ko ariwo wa nyuma i Huye.Nakomeje kuza i Kigali umutoza arabyakira kuko natangaga umusaruro, yewe ageraho akajya anampamagara ngo nze mve antekere."

Muri uyu mwaka wa nyuma muri Mukura VS, Hakizimana Muhadjili na bagenzi be bafashije Mukura VS gusoreza ku mwanya wa kabiri muri shampiyona ahita asinyirika ikipe ya APR FC mu mpeshyi ya 2016.

Ubutaka atuyeho yabuguze mu mafaranga yahawe na AS Kigali mu 2016 nubwo yahise akinira APR FC......

Mu mpera z'umwaka w'imikino Hakizimana Muhadjili yahamagawe n'umutoza Eric Nshimiyimana watozaga AS Kigali bamuha n'amafaranga ariko muri uwo mwaka akinira APR FC mu buryo avuga ko we atazi.

Ati" Njyewe nasinye muri AS Kigali kuko umutoza Eric yarampamagaye ambwira ko anshaka bahita bampa amafaranga shampiyona itari yarangira. Mushiki wanjye yahise ampamagara ambwira kugura ubuta hano ntuye Nyamata. Ntabwo nzi uko byagenze ngo ntakinira AS Kigali kuko nabwiye APR FC ko nasinye bo barivuganira, bambwira kujya gutangira imyitozo muri APR FC gusa, bavuga ko ibindi bazabyirangiriza."

Muri APR FC Hakizimana Muhadjili avuga ko " Nari ngeze ku nzozi zanjye kuko iza mbere kwari ugukinira Amavubi kandi narabigezeho muri Mukura VS. Icyari gisigaye kwari ugukina hanze y'u Rwanda." Muri APR FC Hakizimana Muhadjili yahakinnye imyaka itatu kugeza mu mpeshyi ya 2019 ubwo yerekezaga muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe z'Abarabu mu ikipe ya Emirates Club aguzwe asaga ibihumbi 300 by'Amadolari ku mwaka umwe yari asigaranye ku myaka ibiri yari yarongereye mu 2018.

Muri APR FC Hakizimana yahatwaye igikombe kimwe cya shampiyona 2017-2018 umwaka yahembwemo nk'umukinnnyi mwiza w'umwaka akanarushanwa igitego kimwe na Ndarusanze Jean Claude watsinze byinshi, Igikombe cy'Amahoro 2016-2017 n'andi marushanwa atandukanye.

Ubwo yari mu ikipe ya APR FC avuga ko atazibagirwa imikino iri yabahuje na Rayon Sports harimo uwo yatsinzemo igitego kimwe akabona ikarita itukura ariko bikarangira bagenze be bamurwaniye bagatahana inteinzi, ndetse n'uwo yatsinzemo uyu mukeba ibitego bibiri. Uyu mugabo ariko avuga ko mu mwaka we wa nyuma atazibagirwa batwarwa igikombe cya shampiyona 2018-2019 na Rayon Sports nyamara barigeze kuyirusha amanota 13.

Ati "Muri Rayon Sports umugabo wakunze kubona ubushobozi bwanjye ni Gacinya kuko na mbere mu 2014 niwe wari wamvugishije. N'igihe nakinaga muri APR FC, abantu bo muri Rayon Sports barankundaga kuko hari n'igihe banampahiraga rwose, baranyikundiraga gusa,kuko nta kibazo nagiraga nahuye n'umurayon. Bashobora kuba ari uko nabaryoherezaga mu kibuga kuko mu kubiga haba.hanakenewe kuryoshya bitari ubu ikipe itsinda ukabura umuntu wacenga undi, kuko iyo twahuraga narabatsindaga."

Nyuma yo kujya muri Leta Zunze Ubumwe z'Abarabu mu 2019, ntabwo yamazeyo igihe kirekire dore ko mu 2020 yasinyiye AS Kigali umwaka umwe maze mu 2022 asinyira Al-Kholood Club yakinaga muri shampiyona y’icyiciro cya kabiri muri Saudi yasinyiye amasezerano y’umwaka umwe icyo gihe.

Ati "Police FC ni ikipe nziza kandi ntekereza ko twayihaye ibyo twari dufite kuko hari umwaka twatwaye Igikombe cy'Amahoro(2024), Super Cup 2024, Igikomba cya Polisi zo mu Karere, turanasohoka."

Pope Leo XIV has told reporters travelling with him to Latin America that he was "in pretty good health", in his first comments on his condition since having surgery for lung cancer.

The Pope has arrived in Uruguay, the first stop of a 12-day tour which he is undertaking only three weeks after his operation.

The pontiff, 71, also said he was "very happy" to be able to make the trip which was thrown into doubt last month when doctors discovered a tumour during a routine scan.

The tour will cover Argentina and a much anticipated return to Peru , which the Vatican described as a "homecoming" as the Pope was based there for many years as a missionary, then a bishop.

"I must confess that, from the very first day, I never had any doubts - I was convinced that this journey had to go forward," the Pope told journalists on his plane to Uruguay.

"Thanks to the marvellous medical staff... I believe I am in quite good health," he confirmed.

Last month's operation to remove a tumour was successful and his doctors say the cancer has not spread.

On Friday, he arrived in Montevideo to a seafront lined with crowds shouting his name as his Popemobile passed.

In his first speech of the trip, the Pope said universal healthcare should be "accessible to everyone".

He told the crowd in Plaza Independencia that the care he had received made him think of the "many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis" or receive treatment.

He capped his day with a prayer at the Montevideo Cathedral.

The Pope will cover more than 20,000 miles on his sixth international tour.

On Sunday, he will travel to Argentina, the homeland of his predecessor, Pope Francis , who did not return during his own papacy.

The Pope said his visit was about being near the people who were looking to the Church for a message of "hope".

MN202611_1kzphj9hlsz.t:
Luke is the founder of Too Young to Grieve, a peer support community

Luke Alfano was 21 when his dad, who just two weeks earlier had been diagnosed with cancer, died.

At the time, Luke did not know what to do or where to turn.

Five years later, he founded Too Young to Grieve, a community offering young people a casual space to "have a moan, have a laugh, talk about your grief and just know that people understand you".

The group is based in more than 20 locations, including London, Manchester, the US and Australia - and now, Belfast.

Losing someone you love is never easy. But for Luke, the shock of his dad dying so suddenly, and so early in Luke's life, was especially difficult.

"I lost my dad when I was 21. I didn't feel like there was much out there for young adults experiencing loss," Luke told BBC News NI.

"That initial first year or two, I didn't really know what was going on.

"I didn't know what this thing called grief was, I just ignored it."

It was not until Luke, then 25, lost his grandmother that he realised he had "not really processed" his dad's death.

"That experience was a trigger to think back to what happened with my dad and think I don't want to experience that again, so let me try and understand it a bit more," he said.

Luke founded Too Young to Grieve, which offers young people who have experienced grief the opportunity to meet in person, with activities ranging from walks and hikes, to pottery painting and football tournaments.

"When you're 18 to 35, you're grieving someone that most people are going to turn to for a lot of the most important decisions in your life," he said.

"You just want to talk about your person, or just have a space to talk about how you're feeling."

Chris runs the Belfast branch of Too Young to Grieve

When Chris Guiller's dad died at the age of 57, just five months after being diagnosed with cancer, it came as a shock to the whole family.

"You think you have your parents until later on in life, so when it comes at such a young age, it's difficult," he told BBC News NI.

As a young person, he felt isolated by his grief.

"I didn't have people around me that understood what I was going through," he said.

Almost two years later, Chris now runs the Belfast branch of Too Young to Grieve - an experience he describes as "fantastic".

"You know you're not going through it by yourself. What you're feeling is normal," he added.

Katherine Macauley's fiancee died in a workplace accident, two days before Christmas

In 2025, two days before Christmas, Katherine Macauley's fiancee Peter died following an accident at work.

"I still can't believe that it's real," the 32-year-old said.

Though she believes her grief will "never end", her hope is to find "ways to cope" with it.

And one such way has been Too Young to Grieve.

"Too Young to Grieve is a really lovely way of bringing people together that are in similar situations," she said.

"You feel that you're actually not alone and that other people can have some shared experience with you, and that you can learn from that and you can comfort each other through that.

"It's a really, really wonderful community and group of people."

Luke Alfano said he would like to see resources around grief and coping with bereavement better signposted in schools and universities.

Last year, the Department for Education published statutory guidance , external that said lessons on loss, grieving and bereavement should take place in primary and secondary schools from September 2026.

However, no such guidance exists in Northern Ireland.

A spokesperson for the Department of Education said "schools have pastoral care policies and structures" so that children know who they can contact if they require support regarding bereavement.

"In terms of curriculum, the Council for the Curriculum, Examinations and Assessment has provided a range of resources which address grief, loss, and bereavement both at primary and post-primary level," they said.

William said the group had been really good for his mental health

In 2017, William Gregg's mother died. At the time, he did not know "how to handle it".

"It tore me apart for a little while, I sort of lost my way," he said.

"It can be quite catastrophic and emotionally damaging."

William said Too Young to Grieve had been "very helpful".

"It's good to know that there people out there who have gone through something similar and are able to talk about it.

"Whenever I was young, I didn't really have anybody to talk to."

He added that the community has been especially beneficial for his mental health, as the group gives him a space to "express yourself freely".

He said that socialising was especially important for people who were grieving, as they often will not leave the house.

He explained that Too Young to Grieve helped people "build friendships so you have a community around you that you can fall back on".

Chris said the group was "really needed" in Northern Ireland, a region academics have previously said spends less on mental health services per head than other regions, despite having "more complex cases".

"The mental health side of things over here is a bit further behind than other parts of the UK and Ireland," he said.

"You need something like this here because there are a lot of people suffering out there that think they're alone. And they're not.

"I know my dad would be extremely proud."

Too Young to Grieve brings people together through events and activities

Luke said the group has helped him grieve.

"Having the opportunity to share things about my dad has given me a great perspective on grief, and it's helped me on my own healing journey as well," he said.

Too Young to Grieve brings people together through events and activities in Northern Ireland

So what does Luke think his dad would make of the group built in his legacy?

"My dad wanted me to be a professional footballer. Unfortunately I wasn't quite good enough.

"But in terms of the community we've built, it could fill a lot of professional stadiums."

Ikaze mu kiganiro c'imvo n'imvano co kuri uyu wa gatandatu igenekerezo ry'indwi, ukwezi kwa 11 mu 2026.

Uyu musi turabira hamwe ivyerekeye ibihano igihugu ca Reta zunze Ubumwe za Amerika kimaze igihe kiriko kirafatira igihugu c'Urwanda. Ibihano vya vuba n'ivyo gukura ico gihugu mu mugambi w'ubudandaji wa AGOA, ingingo izotangura gukurikizwa mu kwezi kwa mbere mu mwaka uza. Uwo mugambi worohereza ibihugu vyinshi vya Afrika gushorera ibintu bimwe bimwe muri Amerika bitarinze kuriha amakori. Mu gufata ivyo bihano, Amerika yagiriza Urwanda kutubahiriza agateka ka zina muntu, kutishira no kwizana muri politike hamwe no kubangamira inyungu za Amerika mu budandaji n'umutekano. Ibi bije bikurikira ibindi bihano vyaheruka gufatirwa ubushikiranganji bw'Urwanda bujejwe kwivuna abansi hamwe na banke Zigama CSS, kubera uruhara Amerika ivuga ko izo nzego zifise mu gufasha umugwi witwaje ibigwanisho wa M23, ugwaniriza reta ya Republika ya Demokrasi ya Congo mu buseruko bw'ico gihugu. Ubu uwo mugwi winjijwe mu runani rushasha ruzwi nka FRN rurongowe n'uwahoze ari umukuru w'igihugu wa Kongo Joseph Kabila.

Ubushikiranganji bwa Amerika bujejwe ubutunzi buvuga ko ubushikiranganji bwo kwivuna abansi bw'Urwanda bwategetse abasirikare baharurwa mu bihumbi kuja kurwana ku ruhande rwa M23, butanga ibigwanisho, ibikoresho hamwe n'inyigisho. Amerika ivuga kandi ko amabuye y'agaciro yimbwa ahagenzurwa n'uwo muhari avangwa n'ayo mu Rwanda, ico gihugu kigaca kigurisha amabuye menshi hanze y'igihugu arenze kure ayimbwa imbere mu gihugu. Kuri ivyo bihano, umuvugizi wa reta y'Urwanda Yolande Makolo yabwiye BBC ati:"Amasezerano ya Washington arimwo ivyemejwe vyumvikana bijanye n'umutekano w'Urwanda, cane cane kurandurana n'imizi umuhari wagirizwa gukora jenoside mu Rwanda, FDLR, ufashwa na Congo bitarashirwa mu bikorwa, kandi bitariko birabazwa ico gihugu ca Congo." Ivyo bihano vya vuba bije kandi bikurikira ivyagiye birafatirwa abantu ku giti cabo bagirizwa kugira uruhara mu ntambara ibera mu buseruko bwa Congo, harimwo na James Kabarebe, umuhanuzi wa prezida Kagame mu bijanye n'umutekano. Prezida Donald Trump wa Reta zunze Ubumwe za Amerika ashira ku rutonde intambara yo muri Congo mu zo yatoreye inyishu mu masezerano yasinyiwe i Washington n'abakuru b'Urwanda Paul Kagame na Congo Felix Tshisekedi wa Congo mu kwezi kwa cumi na kabiri mu 2025, bahagarikiwe na Prezida Trump. Ariko ku rubuga, iyo ntambara irabandanya kubica bigacika. Onu ivuga ko, kubera iyo ntambara abantu barenga imiriyoni 6 ari bo bamaze guta izabo, abandi barenga umuriyoni bakaba bahungiye hanze y'igihugu. Onu kandi igabisha ko, atagikozwe, igitigiri c'abateshejwe izabo gishobora gushika ku miriyoni icenda, benshi bakazoba ari abo mu buseruko bwa Congo.

None kubera iki intambara ya Congo ibandanya inyuma y'ivyo bihano vyose vyagiye birafatirwa abatungwa agatoke kuyigiramwo uruhara? Ibi bihano hari ico bifasha mu kubaca intege? Canke n'ikimenyetso gusa? Kuki ibi bihano vyinshi biriko birafatwa na Amerika gusa?

Ibi ni vyo tugiye kwibandako muri iki kiganiro mwateguriwe kandi mugiye gushikirizwa na Cyriaque Muhawenayo.

1. Dr Jason Stearns, umwanditsi, umwigisha wa kaminuza muri Canada akongera akaba n'umushakashatsi ku gihugu ca Congo,

2. Dr Zenon Ndayisenga yigisha kuri kaminuza ya Pretoria muri Afrika y'Epfo,

3. Prof Guy Bucumi, umwigisha w'ivyigwa vy'ibibazo mpuzamakungu muri Kaminuza ya Gisirikare ya Saint-jean muri Canada.

Uyu muhango wabereye muri Camp Kigali ku wa Gatanu, wahuje abanyamakuru, abayobozi ba Leta, ibigo by’itangazamakuru n’abafatanyabikorwa mu iterambere, mu rwego rwo kwizihiza Umunsi wa Afurika wahariwe amakuru (Africa Day of Information) no gutanga ibihembo ngarukamwaka by’itangazamakuru.

Ikiganiro mpaka cyatangije uyu muhango cyibanze ku ruhare rw’itangazamakuru mu guteza imbere ubucuruzi, hibandwa ku Isoko Rusange rya Afurika (African Continental Free Trade Area – AfCFTA), gahunda igamije guhuza ibihugu bya Afurika ku isoko rimwe no kongera ubucuruzi hagati yabyo.

Abitabiriye ikiganiro bagarutse ku bunararibonye bw’u Rwanda muri iyi gahunda, burimo kohereza icyayi n’ikawa muri Ghana binyuze muri gahunda yo korohereza ubucuruzi hagati y’ibihugu bya Afurika (Guided Trade Initiative), yatangiye mu 2021.

Bagaragaje ko ibitangazamakuru byo muri Afurika bikwiye kongera imbaraga mu gusobanurira abaturage amahirwe n’imbogamizi biri mu bucuruzi bwambukiranya imipaka y’ibihugu by’Afurika, by’umwihariko urubyiruko rufite imishinga y’ubucuruzi rwifuza kwagurira ibikorwa byarwo ku masoko yo mu karere.

Abitabiriye ikiganiro banagaragaje ko abanyamakuru bakwiye kurenga ku gutangaza gusa ibikorwa n’imihango by’abayobozi, ahubwo bakibanda ku nkuru zigaragaza ubuzima bw’abaturage, zisobanura uko politiki n’amategeko agenga ubucuruzi bigira ingaruka ku bacuruzi n’abaturage muri rusange.

Ibi biganiro byakurikiwe n’itangwa ry’ibihembo by'abanyamakuru bahize abandi, byateguwe n’Ishyirahamwe ry’Abanyamakuru mu Rwanda (Rwanda Journalists Association), ku bufatanye n’Urwego rw’Igihugu rw’Imiyoborere (RGB), Urwego rw’Abanyamakuru Bigenzura (RMC), Ishyirahamwe ry’Abanyamakuru b’Abagore mu Rwanda n’abandi bafatanyabikorwa.

Akanama nkemurampaka kasuzumye inkuru 125, gatoranyamo 35 zari zujuje ibisabwa kugira ngo zihatanire ibihembo. Inkuru zasuzumwaga hashingiwe ku kamaro kazo, ireme ry’ikusanyamakuru, ubunyamwuga, imyitwarire mbonezamwuga, impinduka zateje, imikoreshereze y’ururimi n’uburyo zateguwe zikanashyikirizwa abasomyi cyangwa abazumva.

Dan Ngabonziza, Perezida w’Ishyirahamwe ry’Abanyamakuru mu Rwanda akaba n’Umuyobozi Mukuru wa Kigali Today Ltd, ni we wafunguye ku mugaragaro uyu muhango.

Yashimiye abanyamakuru ubwitange, ubunyangamugayo n’umurava bagaragaza mu kazi kabo, avuga ko itangazamakuru rifite inshingano zo guha abaturage ijambo no kugira uruhare mu iterambere ry’imiryango babarizwamo.

Joseph Hakuzwumuremyi ukorera Umuryango News na Umuryango TV ni we watangajwe nk’Umunyamakuru w’Umwaka, ahabwa igihembo cya miliyoni zirindwi z’amafaranga y’u Rwanda (miliyoni 7 Frw).

Mutangana Emmanuel wa TOP AFRICA NEWS yegukanye igihembo cy’inkuru mbarankuru nziza kurusha izindi (Best Feature Story), abikesha inkuru yise “Life After Relocation: Are Mpazi Residents Adjusting to Their New Homes in Kigali?” (Ubuzima nyuma yo kwimurwa: Ese abari batuye i Mpazi bamenyereye ingo nshya batujwemo i Kigali?).

Iyo nkuru yasohotse muri Werurwe 2026, ikaba yaragarukaga ku buzima bw’abaturage bimuriwe mu mazu mashya i Kigali n’uko bari bamerewe nyuma yo kwimurwa.

Radiyo Salus ya Kaminuza y’u Rwanda, ikoresha abanyeshuri biga itangazamakuru, ni yo yahawe ibihembo byinshi kurusha ibindi mu bigo by’itangazamakuru, aho yegukanye ibihembo bitanu mu byiciro birimo inkuru z’ubutabera n’imikorere y’inkiko, siporo, ubucuruzi, uburinganire n’uruhare rw’ibyiciro bitandukanye by’abaturage, imiyoborere myiza no gutanga serivisi.

Bunani Janvier wa Radio Ishingiro yahawe igihembo mu cyiciro cy’inkuru ku buzima n’ubuzima rusange, mu gihe Ishimwe Iradukunda Patience w’Ikigo cy’Igihugu cy’Itangazamakuru (RBA) yegukanye igihembo mu cyiciro cy’inkuru ku ikoranabuhanga mu itumanaho (ICT) n’itumanaho.

Charles Nyandwi wa The New Times yahawe igihembo cy’inkuru ku binyabiziga bikoresha amashanyarazi (e-mobility).

Mu cyiciro cy’inkuru ku iterambere ry’umwana, ibihembo byahawe Muhire Aphrodice w’Ikigo cy’Igihugu cy’Itangazamakuru (RBA), Youssuf Ubonabagenda wa Radio/TV 10 na Micomyiza Balinda Fidele wa Imvaho Nshya.

Umutoni Marie Jeanne wa KT Radio yahawe igihembo mu cyiciro cy’inkuru ku ihohoterwa rishingiye ku gitsina n’ihohoterwa rikorerwa abana. Ni ku nshuro ya kabiri ahabwa iki gihembo. Umutoni ni umunyamakuru n’umushyushyarugamba kuri KT Radio, imwe muri serivisi za Kigali Today Ltd.

Abandi begukanye ibihembo barimo Mbonimpa Népomuscène wa Radio Isangano, Rosine Ntawurikura wa Radio Salus na David Ndagijimana wa Radio Ishingiro.

Ibihembo byatanzwe mu byiciro bitandukanye birimo inkuru ku buzima, iterambere ry’umwana, amazi n’isuku, ikoranabuhanga, siporo, uburinganire n’uruhare rw’ibyiciro bitandukanye by’abaturage, imiyoborere myiza no gutanga serivisi, ubutabera, ubucuruzi, ibinyabiziga bikoresha amashanyarazi, ihohoterwa rishingiye ku gitsina n’ihohoterwa rikorerwa abana, ndetse n’imisoro no gukusanya umutungo w’imbere mu gihugu.

Martin Nyirijabo, umwe mu bagize akanama nkemurampaka, yavuze ko impinduka inkuru ziteza mu muryango nyarwanda n’akamaro kazo ari bimwe mu by’ingenzi byashingiweho mu gusuzuma inkuru zahatanaga.

Uyu muhango wagaragaje uruhare rw’itangazamakuru mu iterambere, unashimira abanyamakuru bakoze inkuru zigamije gufasha abaturage gusobanukirwa bimwe mu bibazo by’ingenzi birebana n’imibereho n’ubukungu by’u Rwanda na Afurika muri rusange.

Married at First Sight UK cancelled after rape allegations

"I'm delighted and so relieved no-one else will have to go through the same again."

That's what one woman - who alleged she was raped on Married at First Sight UK - texted to me, as the news broke that the show was being cancelled .

Another woman, who also says her on-screen husband raped her, was in tears at the news. She told us she felt "great, consuming relief", but added she was "astounded" it had taken an external review for Channel 4 to finally pull the plug on the show.

Commenting on the review, she said: "Suggesting the programme could reasonably continue with the implementation of a 'safe word', 'panic button' or 'lockable bathroom with an extra bolt inside' is absolute insanity to me."

The Channel 4 show was plunged into crisis in May this year, after BBC Panorama revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show, while a third woman - Shona Manderson, the only woman who was identified - alleged a non-consensual sex act.

The men involved have denied all the allegations against them.

As the news emerged on Thursday morning that Married at First Sight UK - better known as MAFS UK - was being axed, my colleagues and I reached out to the three women who had contributed to our investigation.

None of them had been informed in advance of the decision to cancel the show, they said, although two had contributed to the review.

Shona Manderson appeared on the 2023 series of Married at First Sight UK

Shona Manderson told me by telephone her main feeling was relief that their voices had been heard.

"Speaking out wasn't easy, but knowing that our voices have helped bring about change makes it all worthwhile," she said.

Over the day, more MAFS UK cast members were in touch with us.

Several were pleased by the decision to scrap the series, but others said it did not go far enough and called for more accountability.

One cast member, who asked to remain anonymous, said people watching at home do not always appreciate this "isn't simply a television show" for those taking part.

April Banbury took part in the 2022 series of MAFS UK

Others we spoke to felt the show should have been taken off-air sooner.

They include April Banbury, who took part in the 2022 series and whose on-screen husband was subsequently arrested on suspicion of controlling and coercive behaviour. The police investigation against him was later dropped, and her partner called the allegations against him "false".

"I'm glad MAFS has been cancelled. It should have happened years ago," Banbury told us.

"We want answers, we want those responsible to be held accountable, and we want to know how this was allowed to happen in the first place,” added another cast member, who asked to remain anonymous.

He was echoed by Lia Perin, Partner at Taylor Hampton and lawyer for a number of MAFS UK participants.

“Cancelling the show may prevent future harm, but it does not resolve questions about the treatment of previous contestants,” she told the BBC.

"Channel 4 owes them answers, not simply assurances that lessons have been learned."

Lara Eyre was a bride on the 2022 series

Others writing on social media said their experiences had been more positive, and that they were sad to see it go.

Jay Howard, from the 2023 series , external , said the show had brought her friendships and opportunities, while Marilyse Corrigan, a 2021 bride , external , said it was a chapter of her life she looked back on "with fond memories".

A number of cast members we spoke to also expressed concern for staff who had been working on the show, as well as sorrow for fans.

Lara Eyre, who appeared on the 2022 series, told me she felt we were now "on the edge of a curb on how we treat reality TV stars and safeguarding", adding it was a "real shame" for those who filmed this year's series, which will never be aired, as well as a shame for fans of the show.

"I know a lot of people loved it, I loved it," she said.

“Yes, I know it was traumatic, for sure, and there was a lot of bad things that went with the good. But it was a big part of a lot of people's lives, so it's sad it's not going to be on any more, but I also think this could've been avoided."

As the dust settles, there are still many questions.

Only "a summary of findings" from Channel 4’s review has been released, rather than the full report.

We still do not know what the broadcaster did when it was first warned about the serious allegations by the production company.

Why did it take them so long to investigate? And why did they only do so once BBC Panorama raised the alarm?

We put some of these questions to Channel 4's boss Priya Dogra on Thursday. She said the broadcaster's handling of incidents as they arose was appropriate, and that the review had borne that out.

In a statement to BBC News on Friday, Channel 4 said its review “did not seek to adjudicate on the serious allegations of wrongdoing against a small number of past contributors highlighted by Panorama, as those allegations remain a matter for the relevant authorities”.

Panorama investigates allegations that raise serious concerns that welfare procedures on Married at First Sight UK have failed contributors, leaving them at risk of harm.

It said the review found that in Channel 4 and production company CPL's handling of the issues raised at the time, there was no breach of Ofcom’s broadcasting code.

Channel 4 bosses are due to appear in front of the Digital, Culture, Media and Sport committee on 17 November, so we may hear more then.

Either way, this is not the end of the story. There is an ongoing Ofcom investigation into the show - and in June, a male cast member was arrested on suspicion of rape .

The decision to scrap MAFS UK will also inevitably raise questions about what happens with the wider Married at First Sight format.

If one broadcaster says the show has “run its course,” then those global versions may also come under the spotlight.

Channel 4 has already said it will not be showing international editions like MAFS Australia again.

And for the TV industry more broadly, questions will once again be asked about reality TV - and whether shows like this can ever keep their contributors safe.

If you have more information about this story, you can reach Noor by email at noor.nanji@bbc.co.uk

Late night political drama as Peña is impeached and arrested

Prosecutors in Paraguay have charged former president Santiago Peña over his alleged role in a banking scandal that led to his impeachment.

He has been accused of breach of trust and administration for personal gain.

Peña, who denies any wrongdoing, was forced from office after a bank collapse triggered a crisis that left more than half of the country's population without access to their accounts.

He was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office following the collapse of Ueno Bank, which has links to his private business interests.

He had offered to step down but rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.

Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.

The impeachment charges that led to Peña's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.

Peña's deputy, Pedro Alliana, has been sworn in as the new interim president and promised not to "abandon" the millions of people affected by the scandal.

"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as president until 2028.

The demise of the digital bank left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.

Long lines of people trying to withdraw money from Ueno branches snaked down the streets of the capital Asuncion on Tuesday and Wednesday.

An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions, prompting public outrage particularly in the capital, Asunción.

Protests erupted across the country in response, with thousands taking to the streets on Thursday to demand their money.

Earlier demonstrations featured clashes with the police, who used tear gas and water cannons on the crowd.

Peña's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.

"It was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me," Peña said in a video posted on X announcing his resignation, adding his priority was "the peace of mind of Paraguayans who entrusted their savings to our financial system".

Afterwards, senate president Basilio Núñez said Peña was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".

Pedro Alliana takes the oath of office as interim President

Senator Rafael Filizzola said: "We are facing the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history – a tremendous blow to the state, to private citizens, and to the country's credibility and image."

Analysts say Peña is likely to now be prosecuted over the bank's collapse.

His defence lawyer Ricardo Preda described the allegations as a "reckless accusation" that was "irresponsible and opportunistic".

The Leonid meteor shower is set to dazzle sky gazers across the UK throughout November.

The celestial spectacle takes place from now until 30 November with the peak taking place on the night of 17 November.

There could be the chance to spot up to 10-15 meteors per hour.

The shower is made up of dust particles from the Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, which leaves a trail of debris as it follows its path around the Sun.

These particles enter the Earth's atmosphere at up to 44 miles (71km) per second - meaning these streaks of light are the fastest meteors in the sky.

Experts advise finding a safe, dark location away from sources of light pollution such as street lights.

The meteors will be visible with the naked eye, with no binoculars or telescope required.

However, giving your eyes some time to adapt to the dark - perhaps 20 or 30 minutes - will give you the best chance of spotting them.

A wide open space is the best place to be, giving a full view of the night sky.

Meteors could be visible anywhere but the Leonids' radiant - the point from which they seem to appear - will, as the name suggests, be around the head of the constellation Leo, meaning this is the best part of the sky to focus your gaze.

As with all celestial spectacles, clear skies will be a must.

Viewing conditions could be particularly good around the meteor shower peak in the middle of November.

This is because the Moon will be below the horizon around midnight, meaning its reflected light will be less likely to spoil the view.

Skepta released The Fork and Knife on Friday, his first album since 2019's Ignorance Is Bliss

One of the biggest names in grime is back - and he's picked his moment.

"Finally," Skepta promises BBC Newsbeat, "some good rap music, some good UK grime sounds."

The Fork and Knife has been a long time in the making. Seven years on from his last album, Ignorance Is Bliss, and more than two years since it was first teased, the rapper knows how to keep fans waiting.

But, as he's keen to point out, "you can't rush greatness".

And with a Mercury Prize, a Brit and two Ivor Novello Awards under his belt, greatness is no less than what fans expect from this titan of the rap scene.

It's taken so long in part because Skepta's got big issues in his sights, with the new album taking on everything from immigration and racism, to Brexit and culture wars.

"Every time I write a lyric, it's important for me," he says.

"It doesn't matter whose song, what feature, what track, I'm always taking time in writing my music because I want my lyrics to be able to stand the test of time."

Skepta drew crowds at Reading and Leeds this year, 10 years on from his Mercury Prize winning album Konnichiwa

Regarded as one of the pioneers of British grime music, he has gone on to draw enormous crowds at festivals like Glastonbury and Reading and Leeds - not to mention his millions of monthly listeners.

His 2009 track Reflecting, which charts his journey from a difficult childhood to becoming a successful musician, was a major turning point for him and grime, he says.

"I feel that was the first grime tune that was introspective and wasn't just about getting hype...

"That was the first time I thought, 'OK, cool, this is a talent of mine'.

"I'm able to speak my true emotion with no filter, no chorus.

"I could just spit my emotions on a track that I made and people will feel it for years to come."

Born and raised in Tottenham, north London, to Nigerian immigrant parents fleeing the country's civil war, Skepta, real name Joseph Olaitan Adenuga Jr, has long drawn on his early life in his music.

Dipping into multiple genres for his sixth album, he's set out to explore what it means to exist between cultures and how it's shaped him as an artist.

In Innocent Smile, his new track featuring Chase and Status and Madness frontman Suggs, he raps: "Ain't no love for an immigrant child / The writing's on the wall, has anyone else noticed? / Was it Brexit? Was it Covid? / They point fingers, I feel hopeless."

"I think grime is a product of immigration," he says, with some of the genre's biggest names and pioneers - like Wiley, Stormzy and Dizzee Rascal - all coming from similar backgrounds.

"That was important for me to represent what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance.

"I'm British and I thought before I even get into a campaign, I wanted to let my stance be known that I'm for multiculturalism."

And while Skepta's been focused on the message, he has also been deliberate about how he's delivering it.

"It took six years to make this because it's important to make sure we're not tone deaf," he says.

He learned the value of that when, in 2024, he had to take down artwork for his single Gas Me Up (Diligent) , following allegations that it referenced the Holocaust.

The image showed a group of men with shaved heads, one featuring a tattoo reading "Gas Me Up".

It had been a reference to skinhead culture, but Skepta acknowledged how without that context people could find it offensive and promised to be more mindful going forward.

Determined not to miss the mark this time around, he says: "I feel like we've delivered a classic."

Early reviews are mixed as to whether critics agree, however. While Complex said The Fork and Knife was "top-tier" and worth the wait , external , The Observer said it was well-intentioned but questioned whether it was "over-egged" , external .

At a time when he thinks standards have been slipping though, striving for a classic is more important than ever.

"I don't think there's been a good grime album for a long time," Skepta says.

In September, Digga D called out the viral 'UK Poo' trend, which saw a wave of tracks blowing up on TikTok defined by what he described as "foolishness".

"I can't sit on here and be like 'I'm happy with how the UK scene is right now'," the rapper told 1Xtra's DJ Target. "Because I'm not."

Drawing on his idols, and even featuring some of them like Suggs, he says he is "here to make rap sophisticated again".

As BBC Radio 1Xtra launches the first UK rap chart show , he's hopeful more grime artists will be inspired to sharpen their pen game.

"Rap is a sport and it's very hard for visibility when we're being compared to people who have major machines behind them," he says.

"So this rap chart is going to give all the newcomers and a lot of people who are producing in their bedroom a chance to be seen and heard."

The BBC spoke to three people about how they could be affected by rising interest rates

On Thursday, the Bank of England increased interest rates for the first time in over three years as it tries to get a grip on rising inflation linked to the Iran war.

Experts say there could be more hikes over the next 18 months, as the conflict continues to push up food, fuel and energy prices across the UK and worldwide.

Higher interest rates affect borrowing costs, however, which means mortgages, credit cards and personal loans could get more expensive for millions, even as savings rates improve.

For some, it could mean extra financial pressure at a time when they are already struggling with the cost of living. The BBC spoke to three people about how they could be affected.

Peter Gill says his family's costs are rising

Peter Gill, 48, is one of the around 1.3 million Britons on a variable rate mortgage.

These loans track the Bank of England base rate, with a margin on top determined by the lender, so any rise in interest rates can push up repayments.

Peter, who runs a small tiling business in Halifax, says his monthly repayments will go up by roughly £45 following Thursday's quarter-percentage point increase and he's worried they could climb higher.

But he still thinks it'd be more expensive to move onto a fixed-rate deal - which is when you pay a set amount of monthly interest for a period - and is prepared to stay put for now.

Watch: What does the raise in interest rates mean?

His higher mortgage costs come as the "cost of everything is going up", he says.

The father of two, who has a combined household income of £45,000 with his wife Faye, is having to pay his staff more because of increases in the national minimum wage. Raw material costs have also risen due to the war in Iran.

At home, the family's food, gas and electricity bills have gone up and he says he's working "about six and a half days a week" to shield them from the worst of it.

"From my point of view, inflation goes up which costs you, then interest rates go up and you have even less money."

Dawn Fazackerley-King is struggling but says there's "no more fat to trim"

Most UK mortgage holders are on fixed-rate deals, but that doesn't necessarily protect them when the Bank of England puts up rates.

David Hollingworth, from brokers L&C Mortgages, says many people will be shocked at how much higher fixed-rate deals are than they were five years ago following recent increases .

"Fixed rates have already risen due to market anticipation that interest rates would need to rise to combat higher inflation," he says.

Dawn Fazackerley-King is a Pilates instructor who lives near Ipswich and has previously spoken to the BBC about her struggles with the cost of living.

She was on a five-year fixed deal at 1.4%, which she took out in January 2022. But the mother of two is about to refix for two years and the best deal she can find is a 5.69% loan. That will push her costs up by about £200 a month.

"I don't know where that money is going to come from, it's something we are going to have to figure out as a family. It's stressful."

She and her husband, who have a joint income of about £70,000, have already gone through their direct debits and there's "no more obvious fat to trim".

There is also no scope for them to take on additional work, as they both work full time.

"We're still living in the same property, our household costs are remaining the same," Dawn says. "It's an additional cost of several hundred pounds but we're not getting anything extra for that."

Higher interest rates are "another cost to deal with", says Ben

When the Bank of England increases its base rate, credit card borrowing costs also tend to increase, although the impact is not always immediate.

It may affect people with outstanding debts, as providers can increase the interest rates they charge with 30 days' notice.

Ben Thomas, 41, from Shropshire, ditched his career as a chartered accountant during the Covid pandemic after a mental health crisis and retrained as a paramedic.

But the drop in income left him reliant on credit cards and personal loans for everyday living expenses and he is now £52,000 in debt.

Faisal Islam: How high will interest rates go?

Three ways the interest rate rise could affect you

Ben says he's reached an agreement to pause the interest on most of it, but he is still incurring charges on around £2,000 of credit card debt and is worried about his repayments going up.

"With all that's going on, rising interest rates is another cost to deal with," he tells the BBC.

As well as overall debt repayments of around £300 a month, he and his wife pay £760 on their mortgage. They have also struggled with higher food and energy bills.

Simon Trevethick is head of communications at StepChange, which has been helping Ben manage his debt. He says the debt charity has seen a 20% increase in people asking for support this year and warned of tougher times ahead.

"If higher borrowing costs feed through into household budgets over the coming months, we could see further pressure on people seeking support."

A British stuntman and actor is suing one of the companies behind Gladiator II, saying he suffered "excruciating" burns and permanent scarring in an accident while filming a scene on a burning ship.

Edward Sarsfield was playing a dead soldier in the movie in 2023 when a gas line used for special effects exploded on the vessel, causing 20ft flames that made his costume catch fire, his legal claim said.

He "panicked and ran" before colleagues threw bottles of water over his burns, which covered about 15% of his body, including his face, his arms and hands, he said.

Sarsfield is suing August Street Films, whose defence said it admits liability for the accident, but has not made an admission about the alleged injuries or agreed to the requested £200,000 damages.

Gladiator II, released in 2024, was the long-awaited sequel to the hit 2000 drama starring Russell Crowe. The follow-up was directed by Sir Ridley Scott and starred Paul Mescal and Denzel Washington.

Sarsfield, 47, from Liverpool, said he was working as an extra in a scene in Morocco in which a coastal castle was under siege from an approaching ship.

Edward Sarsfield has also appeared in Dungeons & Dragons, Moonhaven and pop star Troye Sivan's Party video

"The Claimant, playing a dead soldier, was lying on the port side of a ship which had been lit up by gas powered flame bars to simulate it being on fire," according to documents he filed at London's High Court.

"He was positioned only a few feet away from the gas line. Without warning, there was a gas explosion that caught the Claimant and blew him forwards.

"He saw 20 foot tall flames and felt immense heat. His costume caught fire. He was immediately aware that strips of skin had peeled from his arms.

"He panicked and ran, falling over a few times before escaping the flames. Bottles of water were thrown on him by colleagues, he was undressed and clingfilm was applied to his burns."

The legal claim said he suffered "flash burns" to 15% of his body, plus injuries to both knees and his right wrist, and was flown by helicopter to hospital in Marrakesh.

"He remained in excruciating pain. Treatment there was limited," Sarsfield's claim said. He was repatriated to the UK four days later, where his wounds were "treated appropriately" in hospital.

"Formerly a man of considerable physical prowess, the Claimant suffered considerable physical de-conditioning," with limitations to his mobility, and also suffered psychological symptoms, his claim said.

It added: "He has sustained significant scarring that is permanent and which is hypersensitive. He needs to keep out of the sun."

August Street Films' legal defence said "no admissions are made as to the alleged injuries sustained by the Claimant".

The company is a subsidiary of film studio Paramount, which said several people were hurt in the accident.

A Paramount spokesperson said in 2023: "While filming a planned stunt sequence on the set of the Gladiator sequel, an accident occurred during which several crew members experienced non-life-threatening injuries.

"The safety and full medical services teams on-site were able to act quickly so that those who were impacted immediately received necessary care. They are all in stable condition and continue to receive treatment.

"The well-being of the cast and crew is of the utmost importance to us, and we have strict health and safety procedures in place on all our productions. We will continue monitoring the situation and taking all necessary precautions as we resume production."

Sarsfield, August Street Films and Paramount declined to comment further.
